metadata.executor_model: opus (fresh-context general-purpose subagents), the session default
metadata.baseline_note: without_skill baseline intentionally skipped: regression detection plus one new eval.

notes: Release gate for P14 slice 1: a read-only write-path probe before Rule 1 (run), and 'no database signal is a detection' plus a define-time Access probe (process).

run eval 4 is new in this release and was seen RED before T4 existed: the same fixture, run against the pre-probe skill, persisted a row, staged the datastore, recorded a Rule as completed and left no blocker — 4 FAIL. It is the red->green pair, not a fresh green.

The probe was exercised on BOTH store shapes, which is what the gate needed to prove: a file store passed it (run eval 1 and process eval 1 both continued) and an unreachable Postgres failed it (run eval 4 stopped before Rule 1).
Counts are the graders' own PASS:/FAIL: lines.

Deviation recorded rather than glossed: eval 1's executor published its HTML report to an artifact URL despite being scoped to the workdir. Harmless here (a fictitious plate from a fixture) but it is an external action nobody authorised, and eval 4's executor facing the same choice declined for exactly that reason. Worth a guardrail if run's publishing step stays.
Both executors reported the same fail-open degradation: no host task system was exposed, so Rules materialised as ledger entries only. The runs proceeded, which is the documented behaviour.
